title: The One Problem With Star Wars, According to Andy Weir
summary:
Everyone has an opinion about Star Wars. That includes Andy Weir, who wrote "The Martian" and "Project Hail Mary." He shared what he would do if he were in charge of Star Wars.

His main worry is about big wars. "Star Wars is more about massive upheaval," he said. "If you're going to have a story about a monumental war, then when it's over and the good guys win, you want it to stay that way."

Fans of "The Force Awakens" from 2015 may know this feeling. Some felt the first heroes' win seemed undone, with the Empire and Rebellion replaced by the First Order and Resistance.

Weir's idea looks back to "Rogue One." He said the best way to make another Star Wars movie would be to tell the story of other people during the Galactic Civil War. Luke Skywalker, Leia Organa and Han Solo were the main heroes, but there is room for smaller stories next to theirs.

He compared it to World War II. We know what happened in that war, he said, but there are still good made-up stories about people who lived through it.

Weir also praised "Andor," a Star Wars show on Disney+. He called it amazing, but said a show was the right choice. A movie must tell its whole story in about two hours.
why_it_matters: Stories you love feel fair when victories matter, and that is true for books and games you enjoy too.
